scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
Agent researched a disjoint batch; integration and structural checks are not independent historical certification.
Imported border coordinates remain unchanged. Historical events and map coverage are distinguished in prose; see batchIdentityNotes for conflicts.

proposedOverrides.summary: Regional Dorset histories with a clearly marked atlas endpoint.

batchIdentityNotes: Dorset is retained as the exact archaeological atlas label, not treated as a self-name, uniform people, language, nation, state, or polity.
Tuniit in Inuit oral histories, archaeological Dorset, earlier Paleo-Inuit categories, Thule archaeology, and living Inuit identities remain related but distinct.
Regional chronologies in Newfoundland, Labrador, Nunavik, Baffin Island, the High Arctic, Victoria Island, and Greenland are not collapsed into one phase.
The exact map has four decoded geometry signatures and contracts sharply in 1279; those editorial seams are not historical borders or synchronized events.
Direct finds, radiocarbon dates, isotopes, ancient DNA, experimental analogy, Inuit knowledge, and interpretation remain separate evidence types.
No contemporaneous written-language sample is supplied because no securely attributable Dorset-authored text is known.
The 1492 endpoint is an atlas removal, not a dated extinction; the override keeps fell null and invents no single successor chain.
